neighbours.label: persistence against expectation: a place, state or practice that still remains or survives (one of the last wild places, still liquid, continue to be, there could still be), as opposed to the same frames stating a superlative, a change or a plain fact
fire: The island is one of the last refuges of the giant tortoise.
Two hours after the storm, the basement was still flooded.
In some villages, families continue to arrange marriages for their daughters.
Surprisingly, there could still be live shells buried in the old battlefield.
These hills hold some of the last untouched forests in the country.
Even after a week of sun, the snow on the north slope was still deep.
Across much of the region, farmers continue to plough with oxen.
The valley shelters one of the last herds of wild horses.
quiet: The island is one of the largest producers of sugar cane.
Two hours after the storm, the basement was dry and clean.
In some villages, families arrange large feasts for weddings.
Surprisingly, there were several old coins buried in the field.
These hills hold some of the tallest trees in the country.
After a week of sun, the snow on the north slope had melted.
Across much of the region, farmers now plough with tractors.
The valley shelters a small herd of dairy cows.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.8 on the noun or verb of 'one of the last X', 'still <state>', 'continue to'; superlatives ('largest'), completed change and plain facts below 0.1
notes: Card: peaks ' last' x3, ' still' x3, 'there could be', 'remaining open', 'still really liquid', 'continue'. The + pole suppresses ' still'. Probe: 'one of the last wild places left' 0.776, 'there could still be such hunger' 0.461, 'still liquid' 0.340, 'girls continue to be kept out' 0.310, 'there remained a deep distrust' 0.109; 'one of the largest cities' 0.006, 'centre was firm and golden' 0.008, but 'in this day and age we can fly' 0.238, so the 'in this day and age' frame leaks and near misses avoid it.
